missionPremise: The map tools are demos rather than instruments. Operator QA pass, verbatim: 'the measuring tool there are a few issues. There is no stop or go back. Once you measure in one direction there is a continuation of measuring and it keeps going. If you hit trash it deletes all measurements that you made. There needs to be an undo section. You can not measure length and width together its a single measurement... Even when you double click it does not allow you to place a new line.' Plus 'How do i make the tools disappear so I can read this', 'In the mobile version when i pull up the menus and make a selection the menu needs to collapse', and 'Screen flickers when sizing down'. Source: _dispatches/2026-08-18_ss-w4_dispatch.md. Contract binding: _catalog/parcel_fact_sheet_contract/CONTRACT_RULES.md (frozen), read before any edit.
completionPredicate: A stranger can, on the Smart Site map: take a length and a width as two separate measurements; finish a measurement by double-click, Enter or Esc; undo the last point; delete one measurement without losing the others; read a drawn shape's area in square feet; collapse or hide the floating panels; record a note against a spot and come back to it; and, on a phone, make a selection inside a sheet and have the sheet get out of the way. Every one of those is now expressible in the code and pinned by a test that has been shown to fail when the behaviour is removed. What a merged PR CANNOT establish is that it works on the deployed surface — code-done is not customer-done, and this lane does not deploy.

entries.why: The lane's centre of gravity. Measure had NO committed list and NO commit path (draw had both), so exactly one measurement could exist — the direct cause of 'you can not measure length and width together'. onMapDblClick popped a vertex and never committed, the cause of 'it keeps going' and 'even when you double click it does not allow you to place a new line'. The only removal operation was clearAll(), the cause of 'if you hit trash it deletes all measurements'. Added: committed measurements with ids, finish(), undo(), removeMeasurement/removeShape/removeNote/removeMarker, clearMeasurements/clearShapes, per-segment legs plus running total, area and square footage on measure AND draw, a note tool with parcel scope, setHighlight, and Esc/Enter/Backspace/Ctrl-Z bindings that make the readout's promise true.

The Property Explorer panel. Added collapsible Tools / Results / Layers sections, a minimise and a hide-all control, a results list where each item is removable on its own and hovering a row haloes its geometry on the map, a note editor, a Location tool that flies to the fix and surfaces a denied permission instead of sitting inert, and the mobile rule that activating a tool dismisses the sheet it was activated from.

Command Center's split toolbar drives the SAME controller, so the instrument rebuild had to reach it or CC would silently keep the broken tool. Added the note slot, finish/undo/clear-all row, a results list, and a collapse control.
The other floating panel in the stack. Added a collapse control and moved its z-index onto the shared table.

NEW. One z-order table plus a panel-dismiss event channel. Hand-written z-index literals had no table saying which panel wins, which is the two-implementations-of-one-rule shape DEV_PROCESS 2.4 names. MEASURED at base 5bf06ec, counting rule: occurrences of the string 'zIndex:' in non-test .ts/.tsx files under apps/ and packages/ — 33 occurrences across 15 files. In map-chrome space specifically (PE browse chrome, PE workbench/App overlays, and the shared renderer chrome) it is 17 across 7 files; the remaining 16 sit in Command Center's CountyManifestGrid and LiveMapTile and in PE's paywall / sign-up / share / chat overlays. This lane converted 13 sites in the 5 files it owns onto MAP_PANEL_Z (mobile-layout 7 of 8 — the eighth is the literal string "auto", not a stacking value; MobilePanelContext 2; MapToolset 2; MapTools 1; LayersControl 1). Still hand-written and OUT of this lane's ownership: MapCornerChrome.tsx 2, Workbench.tsx 1, App.tsx 2. The event channel exists because the map chrome lives in the shared package and the mobile sheet state lives in the app, and neither may import the other.
Additive exports only, so the new symbols are reachable from the package barrel.

The context exposed openSheet and NO close primitive at all, so a sheet could not dismiss itself. Added closeSheet, toggleSheet, dismissSheetIfUnchanged, auto-collapse on in-sheet selection, tap-the-active-tab-to-close on the bottom nav, and a listener for the map chrome's dismiss event.

Re-exports the shared z table and replaced its seven stacking literals with it (the eighth zIndex site is the string "auto", which is not a stacking value). Holds the PURE dismissal rules (shouldDismissSheetOnClick, nextSheetOnDismiss, nextSheetOnToggle) so the decision is testable in this app's node-only vitest.
NEW. 28 cases against the controller, each written from a defect the operator reported.
NEW. 17 cases on the dismissal rule, the navigation guard, and the existence of the close primitive.

dispatchItemDisposition.evidence: Its own tool slot (not Location's, not the marker's), its own source and colour, a pending state so an untexted note reads as unfinished rather than silently blank, per-note removal, and a parcel scope stamped from the host. Round-trips through the existing getDrawings() dossier seam with text + scopeId + scopeLabel, so it persists through machinery that already exists rather than a second store.
dispatchItemDisposition.gap: The dossier overlay is READ-ONLY by contract, so a restored note redraws as a point and is not editable again. Re-hydrating live tool state from a saved dossier is a different seam and is left open.

dispatchItemDisposition.evidence: closeSheet / toggleSheet / dismissSheetIfUnchanged added — the primitive the API never had. Auto-collapse fires on an in-sheet selection, is deferred one tick, and is applied with a functional update that only collapses when the active sheet is still the one that was open, so an in-sheet control that navigates elsewhere always wins. Tapping the active bottom-nav tab is a second way out. Activating a map tool from the layers sheet dismisses it via the window event.

dispatchItemDisposition.item: 7. Resize flicker — confirm or refute, do not edit

resizeFlickerVerdict.briefingClaim: ExplorerMap.tsx renders the card as two different subtrees, one guarded by isMobile and one by !isMobile, at the 768px breakpoint, so drag-resizing across that boundary unmounts and remounts on every crossing.
resizeFlickerVerdict.verdict: CONFIRMED AS FAR AS IT GOES, but it does not account for what the operator described.
confirmedEvidence: apps/property-explorer/src/browse/ExplorerMap.tsx:1496 `{card && !isMobile && (` renders InspectCard directly; :1509 `{card && isMobile && (` renders MobileSheet wrapping InspectCard. Two distinct sibling positions in one children array; React reconciles children by position, so crossing the breakpoint nulls one slot and mounts the other. InspectCard therefore unmounts and remounts.

apps/property-explorer/src/browse/mobile-layout.ts:PE_MOBILE_BREAKPOINT_PX = 768; useMobileViewport.ts drives it from a matchMedia change listener, which fires once per crossing rather than continuously.

MapToolset returns a structurally different tree on each side of the breakpoint (mobile: a hidden div plus a fixed sheet; desktop: the floating bubble cluster), so the toolset panel also remounts at the crossing even when no card is open.
resizeFlickerVerdict.whyIncomplete: A matchMedia crossing is a ONE-SHOT event. Dragging a window from wide to narrow crosses 768 exactly once, so this mechanism produces a single flash, not the continuous 'flickers when sizing down' the operator reported, and it produces nothing at all at widths that never cross 768.

secondMechanism.summary: Every resize re-runs the whole live-layer fetch batch and replaces the overlay data.
chain: packages/map-renderer/src/map-renderer.js:361 — `resizeObs = new ResizeObserver(() => map?.resize()); resizeObs.observe(mapEl);` The container is position:absolute inset:0, so it resizes with the window.
node_modules/maplibre-gl@5.24.0/dist/maplibre-gl-dev.js:71621-71638 — Map.resize() fires movestart, move, resize and then moveend (line 71636).

apps/property-explorer/src/browse/ExplorerMap.tsx:372 — handleViewportChange aborts the in-flight batch and re-issues parcels, FEMA, topography, hydrography and opportunity-zone fetches for the new bbox, then replaces each overlay's data.
secondMechanism.evidenceQuality: Every step is read at source and quoted above. It has NOT been measured live in a browser, so it is a code-path reading, not an observation. Stated as a hypothesis with its basis rather than as a finding.

suggestedFixes.forP39_breakpointRemount: Render InspectCard ONCE, inside a single shell component whose own type does not change, and let that shell branch on isMobile internally. Swapping the shell component type would remount the card just the same; keeping one stable element position is what stops it.
suggestedFixes.forP39_orP41_refetchStorm: Skip the viewport refetch when the new bbox is CONTAINED in the bbox already fetched. Sizing DOWN always produces a smaller bbox, which is exactly the direction the operator named, so a containment check kills the storm in the reported case while leaving pans and zoom-outs alone.

contradictionsWithTheBriefing.briefingSaid: Three floating panels (Reports and exports, TOOLS, LAYERS) stack over each other with no z-management and no collapse.
contradictionsWithTheBriefing.atSource: TOOLS and LAYERS were already merged into ONE panel (MapToolset) with a bubble that collapses it, as of the 2026-07-29 operator revision. The stack the operator saw is the workbench dock plus that one toolset panel plus the inspect card. The 'no z-management' half is correct and worse than stated: 33 hand-written zIndex sites across 15 non-test source files, values 5 through 40, with no table. See zIndexCountCorrection for the counting rule.
contradictionsWithTheBriefing.consequence: The panel-manager work is therefore section-level collapse, a minimise, a hide-all and a shared z table, rather than the collapse-a-third-panel the briefing implies. Reporting a planner figure as wrong is a successful outcome per DEV_PROCESS 3.2.

contradictionsWithTheBriefing.briefingSaid: The Location tool ... on select it must fly the map to the located point.

The real gaps were that no zoom cap was set, nothing consumed the position, and a denied permission produced no message.
contradictionsWithTheBriefing.consequence: Implemented as a zoom-capped fly on both drivers plus an onLocated seam plus an honest error line, rather than as a new fly on top of an existing one.
